REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOV GOVE A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE RECORDS RELEAS SISNAURE•. DATE: TIME'. MR. JESUS REMO A. GOMEZ President Shelter Concepts Inc. 2/F Stall 12, The North Atrium MC Briones Street, Mandaue City Dear Mr. Gomez: DILG Legal Opinion$k This has reference to your 05 October 2011 letter requesting the Department's opinion on the following: a. Whether Section 3 of BP 220 subsists with the repeal of PD 1185 by RA 9514; and b. Whether the specification for a 0.30 meter fire wall detailed/specified in the 2008 BP 220 IRR is valid and subsisting thereby placing structures constructed under BP 220 outside the ambit of the 2008 Fire Code. We opine that the repeal of PD 1185 by RA 9514 does not render nugatory the standards and technical requirements for economic and socialized housing set under BP 220 and its IRR, as revised. RA 9514 is the law which sets the standard fire prevention and safety measures to all persons and private and public buildings, facilities or structures erected or constructed, in general. On the other hand, BP 220, is the law which specifically set the standard and technical requirements for economic and socialized housing projects. The legal maxim, genera/ia specia/ibus non derogat, i.e., a general law does not nullify a specific or special law, applies in this case. As held in Lichauco & Co. vs. Apostol, 44 Phil, 138 (1922), viz. : "It is a well-established principle of legal hermeneutics that a general law on a subject does operate to repeal a prior special law on the same subject, unless it clearly appears that the legislature has intended by the later general act to modify or repeal the earlier special law. The presumption against implied repeal is stronger when, of two laws, one is special and the other general; and this rule applies even though the terms of the general act are broad enough to include the matter covered by the special statute. ' The rationale for this is explained in De Villa vs. Court of Appeals, 195 SCRA 722 (1991), viz.: 'The reason why a special law prevails over a general law is that the legislature considers and makes provision for all the circumstances of the particular case. The legislature having specially considered all of the facts and circumstances of the particular case in granting a special charter, it will not be considered that the legislature, by adopting a general law containing provisions repugnant to the provisions of the charter, and without making any mention of its intention to amend or modify the charter, intended to amend, repeal or modify the special act. ' This opinion is shared by the Bureau of Fire Protection in its 02 January 2012 letter to the Department, viz. : "With the passage of R.A. 9514, P.D. 1185 was repealed. However, in so far as the repeal is concerned, R.A. 9514 did not provide any provision regarding construction of firewalls which was not provided also even under the Old Fire Code. It is clear now therefore that aside from the fact that BP 220 is a special law as compared to R.A. 9514 being a general one, the repeal of P.D. 1185 by R.A. 9514 does not in any way affect the requirements and specifications of BP 220 regarding the construction of firewalls with respect to economic and socialized housing projects. oon I I onanifir•allu rafiinrl etanHarH and fanhnirnl ranniramanfe fnr

However, the application of BP 220 is without prejudice to the provisions of RA 9514 on matters not inconsistent with the standards and technical requirements for economic and socialized housing set out in BP 220. Both laws should be harmonized keeping in mind the legislature's intent and purpose for the enactment of said laws. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. For your reference, we have attached a copy of the 02 January 2012 opinion on the issue by the Bureau of Fire Protection. Very truly yours, SUS Director LS08,rb QUE IV
